# Review, pass 1 — secret-history-198-199 (§§198–199)

Checked against: packet.md (502 words), conventions.md, the published parts (esp. 151-153, 154-157, 177, 178-181, 194, 196-197) and secret-history-glossary.json. `units.json` was edited in place by script; no `t` was touched (all 84 units re-cut against the packet: 502 words, each once, `p` flags correct, no unit spans two §§). Every morph's trailing [Ming gloss] was compared mechanically with the packet's gloss: all 502 match. Suffix forms and vowel-harmony / "after a vowel/consonant/r/s" labels were checked mechanically against the printed tokens.

Unit numbers are 0-based positions in `sentences` (unit 0 = Merkid irgen daγ̇uližu; unit 36 = Mün hüker žil…, first of §199).

## Findings refused

- Unit 1 i "eldest son": note admits it rests on Ming 大; published §§154-157 render jeke köġün "eldest son". Kept.
- Unit 3 n "recurs three times": bolurun at units 3, 28, 32, 36, i.e. three further times after this one. Correct as written.
- Unit 40 i "When the word is given": a guess, but flagged as such in the note and parallel to the published reading of the same formula. Kept.
- Units 29, 55 (küġün-e vs künesün-e labels "dative" / "dative-locative"): both follow the glossary entries exactly. Kept.
- köġün (not köġü) as lemma in köġud(i)-jer(i)-jen, köġüd-i: the glossary itself calls köġü a spelling of köġün. Kept.
- aldaž- + -žu in aldažu (unit 77): morphologically odd (alda- + -žu is likelier) but it is the glossary lemma for this token, and the Ming 放着 vs earlier 誓 is already flagged. Kept; glosser to broaden.
- Quotation handling (units 4, 29, 37 unclosed Shiratori marks given as reported speech; Daγ̇u … gedkün as the speech; inner single quotes in 33, 58, 78): consistent with conventions and the note on each; the alternative that the mark at Sübeġetei-ji opens a speech running to gedkün is a real possibility but the draft's reading is stated and defensible. Kept.
- ködölžüġüi analysed -žüġüi (glossary: -žü + -ġüi): follows the draft's uniform -žuγ̇ui / -žüġüi treatment, which the glossary also uses for ažuγ̇ui. Kept.

## Remaining doubts / for pass 2 and the glosser

- Known glossary entries that the glosser should broaden for this part: γal (name Γal, not "fire"), josu-γ̇ar (Ming 道理 here), jabudqun (-dqun whole), göreġesün-dür (Ming 野獸), čeriġüdi (-jer after the (i)), gedkün (ge- already in the entry).
- Unit 56 "Keep in mind what lies beyond" (alus sedkižü): alus unknown, Ming 隔越; i is a firm sentence for an uncertain word.
- Unit 61: the 不 in the Ming gloss of sudalbižu may be ülü carried over; the draft's scope ("bridle not fitted and mouth not checked") is a guess, as the note says.
- Unit 49 "I have sent you" (supplied object and speaker) and unit 71 "what need" rest on the Ming alone.
- Unit 7 übül + -že- + -žü is asserted, not hedged; unit 57-60 kemten / aba-dāča link flagged in the note only.
- Quote marks: the whole of 223-436 might be one speech in Shiratori's own marking; pass 2 should check the build output for stray marks.


# Review, pass 2 — secret-history-198-199 (§§198–199)

Checked: every gloss.json entry (127 new, 6 broadened) against the packet's Ming gloss (all trailing [Ming] brackets compared mechanically with the token's gloss), the text and the units' morph lemmas; the known entries used in this part against this part's readings (known-forms.json and the shared glossary); units.json l ↔ i, every note label, quote marks (mechanical count of marks in t, l, i), names against the published parts. Both files edited in place by script (JSON dumped as before; no `t` touched). Unit numbers are 0-based, as in pass 1.

## Gloss entries checked and kept (no change)

All 127 new entries: dictionary forms agree with the unit morph lemmas (mechanical comparison, token by token); grammar labels checked (case, converb, participle, causative, reciprocal, optative, "after s/r/a consonant", harmony); no invented modern forms (Irtysh is the historical name and is marked as the Ming's river-name; Qangli, Kipchak, Chu are the published spellings). Kept although doubtful, and each is labelled "uncertain" in the entry: šiba (stray shot), oloṅki (olon + -ki), bariγ̇uži-ji, boluji, turuγ̇ai/baraγ̇ai, taniγdaqun, kiduqun-i, nemürgen, öṅgekü-jen, činaγ̇un, mösekdükün, aγ̇uγa, hülüdtele, üžüġüren. The four pass-1 broadens γal, josu-γ̇ar, čeriġüdi, aldažu check out (old entry whole, then " · ", then the new reading).

## Units re-checked and kept

- Unit 4, 29, 37: Shiratori's unclosed opening marks stay unrendered; the opening at 37 and at 40 give one closing mark (72). Reading kept (see unit 39 n). Mechanical count: i marks balance (33–34 outer pair; 40–72 outer pair with ‘…’ at 58; 75–82 outer pair with ‘…’ at 78).
- Unit 1 "eldest" (大), 49 "I have sent you", 61 (the 不 belongs to sudalbižu itself in the packet: 不閘口着, so pass 1's doubt about ülü being carried over does not arise; the scope stays a guess, as the note says), 77 "let my word go" (aldažu; the Ming 放着 differs from the earlier 誓; "swear" is not used because the Ming does not say it): kept, notes already hedge.
- Grammar labels in all 84 notes read against the printed forms; vowel-harmony labels in morph glosses checked mechanically against the suffix vowel (no mismatch).

## Remaining doubts

- Units 42–48 (the "become a bird/marmot/fish" run) and 49–50 are the least secure in sense; unit 42's tense (present in i, past in the Mongol) is explained in the note.
- Unit 77: whether aman kelen aldažu is "give one's word/swear" (as in earlier parts) or "let go a word"; the subject of odčuγ̇ui is assumed.
- Unit 12: "put their own troops in order" for žasažu ažuγ̇ui (the Mongol is a continuing past, "were arranging"); i kept the shorter form.
- Build writes the shared glossary: re-running build is safe and gives byte-identical output, but a later change to a NEW gloss.json entry is ignored once it is in the glossary (only __broaden__ keys are overwritten). To change a new entry after a build: `git checkout -- secret-history-glossary.json stories.json`, delete secret-history-198-199.json, edit gloss.json, build again.
